title: Graded DCA same-day run state artifact
description: Structure of the run_state.json artifact written by near_close_dca.build_run_artifacts() / write_run_artifacts() each trading day and consumed by the reporting/dashboard code. Contains no secrets. A run_classification block (see run_classification.schema.json) accompanies every run of the repaired live task 10ce362c (which supersedes the deleted ce16ba6b) so scheduled and manual runs are never confused; it is validated here when present. It is not listed in `required` so legacy/compact artifacts written before this was stamped still validate.

run_classification.description: Authoritative scheduled-vs-manual classification. Validated against run_classification.schema.json when present. Emitted for live scheduled runs; see docs/run_classification.md and config/run_classification.json. As of 2026-07-17 every scheduled 3:20 PM run_state must carry this nested run_classification object, and a scheduled run is confirmed only when this nested object is present and valid; a run_state missing it is a validation discrepancy. (Confirmed by the 3:40 PM watchdog, a46bf007, until it was removed from the schedule entirely on 2026-08-02; now confirmed by 67aa802b's post-trade validation.) Scheduled/manual identity fields live only under this nested object (see docs/run_classification.md); top-level mirror fields are not required by the artifact writers/consumers. It stays out of the top-level `required` list so legacy/compact artifacts written before this was stamped still validate.

run_id.description: Trading day plus HHMMSS, e.g. 2026-07-06-153005. This is the artifact build id; run_classification.run_id is the origin-scoped id used by reporting to include/exclude runs.

generated_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp (America/New_York) when the artifact was built.

broker.description: Execution broker for the run (e.g. robinhood).

recovery_rerun.description: True when this run_state was produced by an automatic failure-recovery attempt of a scheduled live task (morning 42173154, midday a6239dae, afternoon 10ce362c). A recovery rerun reuses the same logical scheduled run directory and keeps the run's scheduled run_classification — it is NEVER reclassified as manual. See the failure_recovery_policy in config/scheduled_tasks.json and docs/run_classification.md#recovery-reruns.

recovery.description: Details of an automatic failure-recovery attempt, present when recovery_rerun=true. Recovery is triggered only by internal persistence, parsing, wrapper-normalization, transient connector throttling, or raw-file write failures that occur AFTER data was fetched; read-only inputs are rerun once, all raw responses are persisted first, and the run is recomputed only from persisted files through the same guarded path. No secrets.

attempt.description: Recovery attempt number. Only one recovery attempt is permitted per scheduled run.

persisted_raw_first.description: True when all rerun raw responses were persisted to disk before any recomputation.

recomputed_from_persisted.description: True when the run was recomputed only from the persisted raw files.

escalated.description: True when the recovery attempt also failed or a safety/account/order rejection occurred and the run escalated instead of retrying further.

blocking_reason.description: Populated when escalated=true: the reason recovery could not complete (recovery failure, or a safety/account/order rejection).

order_submit_status.description: Overall order-submission outcome for the run. 'no_orders_submitted' (added 2026-07-27) is a run that fired, evaluated every ticker, and deliberately submitted nothing: a completed no-order run, neither a failure nor budget exhaustion. Its cause is carried by completion_reason (no ticker qualified on the ladder, so nothing reached the spread gate) or by error_class (candidates reached the spread gate and every one was failed closed there). See config/scheduled_tasks.json:spread_data_availability_policy. 'not_submitted_confirmation_required' means Robinhood review passed but submission was blocked by required post-review user confirmation: the run_state is still valid scheduled-run evidence that the task ran, but carries no order_id and is NOT evidence of an order/fill. 'blocked_placement_phase_unreachable' is the approved terminal state (added 2026-07-22) when the scheduled 3:20 live task planned orders but neither the saved compute module nor the approved fallback placement path (main live placement runner / direct connector) could place them: the run still proves the task fired and keeps planned rows in signals.csv, but is NOT evidence of an order/fill and carries error_class='placement_phase_unreachable'. A compute-only module that plans orders but never places them (error_class='placement_not_implemented_in_compute_module') is NOT a valid terminal state and must not be written as a completed scheduled run. The scheduled 3:20 PM live task always writes a run_state (and updates latest_scheduled_run.json) even when this is not 'submitted'. See docs/run_classification.md and config/run_classification.json.

error_class.description: Machine-readable failure class for a non-clean run. Open-ended free-form concrete code, intentionally NOT a closed enum: constraining it would reject legitimate existing failure-state artifacts. The morning/midday live runners emit 'missing_or_invalid_raw_inputs' on a raw-persistence failure (morning_dca.py), and the scheduled tasks also emit codes such as 'pointer_normalization_failed', 'missing_preflight_artifact', and 'no_incremental_top_up' (see config/scheduled_tasks.json and config/run_classification.json). The 3:20 placement contract (added 2026-07-22) additionally defines two placement-specific codes: 'placement_phase_unreachable' pairs with order_submit_status='blocked_placement_phase_unreachable' (approved terminal state after the fallback placement path was tried and failed); 'placement_not_implemented_in_compute_module' marks the Jul 22 2026 incident state (a compute-only module that planned orders but could not place them) and is NOT a valid terminal state for the pre-authorized scheduled live task -- validate_run_artifacts / the 3:40 watchdog reject it. Other concrete codes such as 'connector_error', 'safety_rejection', 'account_rejection', 'order_rejection', and 'recovery_failure' may also appear. 'scheduled_run_startup_failure' (added 2026-07-27) marks a scheduled live run that raised before reaching any writer; it still writes the complete root-level artifact set, which proves the slot fired but is never order evidence and never valid scheduled evidence. 'degraded_market_data' (added 2026-07-27) marks a zero-order run that completed while market-data providers were raising: its tickers degraded to NO_DATA/manual review rather than being genuinely evaluated, so the result is not a clean ladder no-op and must not be read as one. 'partial_placement_failure' (added 2026-07-27) marks a batch where some orders were submitted and at least one other placement raised. 'scheduled_run_failed_after_submission' (added 2026-07-27) marks a run that raised AFTER at least one order was submitted, kept distinct from the startup class so a consumer grouping by error_class never reports a late post-trade failure as startup trouble. 'missing_spread_data' (added 2026-07-27) is recorded ONLY when candidates actually reached the spread gate and every one was failed closed there; a run where no ticker qualified on the ladder never reached the gate and records completion_reason='no_ladder_candidates' with a null error_class instead. Null/omitted for clean runs and for a completed no-order run.

run_classification_outcome.description: Outcome classification for the run, distinct from the nested run_classification identity object and never a substitute for it (that object stays a non-null object on every scheduled run). 'completed_no_orders' is a run that completed and deliberately submitted nothing; 'failed_after_connector_native_recovery_attempt' is a genuine placement failure after placement WAS attempted; 'failed_scheduled_run_startup' is a run that raised or was blocked before reaching placement at all, kept distinct so reporting cannot misattribute a startup, data, or precondition failure as a broker-placement failure; 'failed_after_partial_submission' covers both a run that raised AFTER submitting at least one order and a partially submitted batch where another ticker's placement failed, so the outcome never contradicts a non-zero orders_submitted_count and a failed placement is never dropped; 'failed_placement' is the manual-run equivalent of failed_after_connector_native_recovery_attempt, since the manual path never runs the scheduled connector-native recovery policy.

completion_reason.description: Why a COMPLETED run submitted no orders. 'no_ladder_candidates' means no ticker qualified on the ladder and same-day top-up rules, so nothing ever reached the spread gate and error_class stays null. 'blocked_before_spread_gate' means candidates DID qualify on the ladder but every one was stopped by a budget/cap/ceiling/duplicate check that runs before the spread lookup, so none carries a spread verdict. 'no_qualifying_orders_after_safety_checks' means candidates reached the spread gate but none cleared every check. 'date_or_holiday_gate_blocked' marks the date/holiday gate stub. Set on a completed_no_orders run; a failed run records error_class instead.

is_trading_failure.description: False for a completed no-order run: a safe skip, valid scheduled evidence that the slot executed, never a missed slot, and never counted as an error in scheduled reliability. True only for a genuine failure.

scheduled_evidence_denied.description: Explicit writer denial that this run_state is valid scheduled evidence, honored by same_day_pointer.derive_valid_scheduled_evidence exactly as artifact_contract_failure is. Set on a synthesized startup-failure artifact: it proves the scheduled slot FIRED but is never order evidence and never scheduled evidence. It lives at the top level rather than inside run_classification because the morning writer seeds run_classification.valid_scheduled_evidence to false as a placeholder and finalizes it FROM that derivation, so honoring the nested field would lock every run to false.

orders_failed_count.description: Placements that raised. Non-zero alongside a non-zero orders_submitted_count marks a partially submitted batch: some orders landed and another ticker's placement failed, so the run is a partial success AND a trading failure. Both facts are recorded; the submitted count and status are never dropped.

orders_submitted_count.description: Orders this run actually submitted. Written on every run, including zero-order runs.

candidates_reaching_spread_gate.description: Candidates that qualified on the ladder and same-day top-up rules and therefore reached the spread gate. Zero means the gate was never exercised, so a missing spread cannot be this run's error_class.

candidates_blocked_missing_spread.description: How many of candidates_reaching_spread_gate were failed closed because their own bid/ask spread could not be proven. Never exceeds candidates_reaching_spread_gate. Spread is never estimated, inferred, or defaulted; only the affected rows fail, and every other ticker keeps being evaluated.

account_number.description: Target broker account number, or null when not bound (e.g. dry-run). No secrets.

raw_input_dir.description: Absolute path to the raw/ directory under this run's artifact dir where every raw Robinhood/Finance/Alpaca/Yahoo connector response used by the run was persisted (normalized to parseable JSON) BEFORE signal computation. Contract added 2026-07-10 after the 3:20 PM escalation: compute reads only these persisted files, never in-memory tool responses. See docs/schedule_manifest.md (RAW DATA PERSISTENCE FIX) and docs/run_classification.md.

raw_inputs_saved.description: Deterministic filenames actually persisted under raw_input_dir before compute (e.g. quotes_batch1.json, historicals_batch1.json, tradability_pre_place.json, portfolio_pre_place.json, orders_after_place.json, place_SYMBOL.json). Empty when raw persistence failed; in that case the scheduled run_state is still written with order_submit_status='not_submitted_error' and no orders.

recovery_from_escalation.description: True when this scheduled run_state was produced by recovering an escalated run (e.g. re-fetching quotes/historicals, persisting raw connector outputs, normalizing output_path pointers, then computing signals) rather than by a clean first-pass execution.

raw_persistence_error.description: Set when raw connector persistence or normalization failed. The scheduled run_state is still written (run_origin='scheduled', manual_run=false, no orders) with order_submit_status='not_submitted_error' rather than escalating without state.

budget_evaluated.description: False when Gate 6 (budget/tier selection) never ran on this fire -- e.g. the seven-slot roster's END_SILENTLY (weekend/holiday, exits at Gate 0), GATE5_DISABLED (exits at Gate 5, before Gate 6), GATE4_EXPECTED_OVERLAP, or an ABORT at Gate 1/2/3/4 (all before Gate 6). budget_tier/daily_cap_usd/weekly_cap_usd are not required in that case, since fabricating a tier that was never actually selected would be worse evidence than omitting it (Codex review: "Define a schema-valid budget for pre-budget exits"). Omitted (or true) for every run that actually reached Gate 6 and selected a tier, matching every artifact written before this field existed -- omission is NOT itself treated as 'unevaluated'; only an explicit false is.

base_buy_amount_usd.description: Legacy alias of base_amount_usd; both are written for backward compatibility.

signal_rows.description: One row per (ticker, source) evaluated during the run.

status.description: 'pending', 'unconfirmed', and 'filled' (added 2026-07-27) were always produced and read by the runners but were missing from this enum, so a candidate row carrying one failed schema validation even though the guards depend on it: near_close_dca._PRIOR_ALLOCATION_STATUSES counts 'filled' as prior same-day allocation, and scheduled_artifacts.ORDER_ATTEMPT_STATUSES treats 'pending'/'unconfirmed' as a placed-or-in-flight order that must be recorded. The enum was out of date, not the data -- remapping these to 'submitted' instead would have changed which rows the same-day top-up guard counts (Codex review).

reviewed_order.description: Broker order-review result captured before submission, present when Robinhood review passed. Populated even when the order was not submitted (e.g. status 'not_submitted_confirmation_required'), so a confirmation-blocked scheduled run still records the reviewed order details it would have placed. Carries no order_id (nothing was submitted). No secrets.

afternoon_desired_amount.description: Same-day top-up guard (scheduled afternoon run only): the full afternoon desired dollar amount before the prior-run offset.

afternoon_decision_price.description: Same-day top-up guard: the afternoon decision price compared against the earlier same-day run's reference price.

prior_same_day_amount.description: Same-day top-up guard: dollars already bought earlier the same day by a morning/manual run for this ticker.

prior_same_day_reference_price.description: Same-day top-up guard: the earlier same-day run's reference price (fill/target/decision price); the afternoon run only tops up when its price is strictly below this.

prior_same_day_run_id.description: Same-day top-up guard: run_id of the earlier same-day run that supplied the prior allocation.

prior_same_day_source.description: Same-day top-up guard: origin (e.g. manual) of the earlier same-day run.

incremental_order_amount.description: Same-day top-up guard: the incremental dollars actually ordered this afternoon (afternoon desired minus prior amount, or 0 when offset/guarded).

top_up_guard_result.description: Same-day top-up guard outcome code for this candidate. same_day_topup_not_lower_or_no_delta is the scheduled afternoon guard's canonical (Jul 24 2026) unified code for a same-day top-up skipped because the price is not strictly lower than the ticker's reference or the recomputed delta is 0; price_not_below_prior_run/no_incremental_difference remain in use by the morning/midday guards for their own sessions. missing_prior_base means a known prior same-day amount had no resolvable first-allocation base (selected_base_amount_usd), so the guard conservatively bought $0 and flagged manual review rather than recompute the base from this run's own price. below_broker_minimum_order_size means the computed top-up was strictly positive but below the broker minimum order size.

top_up_skipped.description: Same-day top-up guard: true when the guard produced no incremental buy.

top_up_manual_review.description: Same-day top-up guard: true when a known prior amount lacked a comparable price so the run conservatively bought $0 and flagged manual review.
